papers.title: Advancing clinical integration in undergraduate dental education through AI-enabled instructional design: a qualitative thematic analysis
abstract: Background: Despite growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in health professions education, qualitative evidence for integarting AI-supported instructional redesign on teaching practices and students' experiences in undergraduate dental education remains limited. The aim of this study was to explore the educational impact of AI-supported instructional redesign of lessons in undergraduate dental education.

Methods: We conducted this inductive qualitative thematic analysis in an undergraduate dental education setting. Existing lessons were redesigned using AI-supported recommendations to strengthen alignment between learning objectives, authentic clinical contexts, and expected clinical outcomes. Data were collected through classroom observations and students' focus group discussions. An inductive thematic analysis was performed, and findings from multiple data sources were curated, collecetd, and triangulated to enhance credibility.

Results: AI-supported instructional redesign transformed teaching by promoting authentic clinical scenarios, clinically oriented discussions, and explicit reasoning activities. Thematic analysis identified four interconnected themes: (1) a shift from teacher-centred knowledge delivery to facilitation of clinical reasoning; (2) transformation from passive attendance to active cognitive engagement; (3) building clinical meaning through authentic clinical contexts and collaborative dialogue; and (4) creating conditions for professional learning through psychological safety. AI functioned as a pedagogical design-support tool rather than replacing the educators' instructional role. Overall, the observed educational changes appeared to arise primarily from the pedagogical redesign enabled by AI-supported planning rather than from students' direct interaction with AI.

Conclusion: This study endorses the role of AI-supported instructional redesign in enriching the existing undergraduate dental curriculum. This approach can potentially help educators align learning objectives, instructional strategies, and authentic clinical contexts. The reported educational modifications reflect primarily the implementation of learner-centred and clinically oriented pedagogical strategies, with AI functioning as a design-support mechanism rather than as a direct instructional agent.

papers.title: The association between age and mortality in men with adult-onset testosterone deficiency is altered by testosterone therapy
abstract: Background: Using the Gompertz-Makeham model, we describe associations between age and the probability of mortality in men with adult-onset testosterone deficiency (TD), stratified by testosterone undecanoate (TU) treatment and type 2 diabetes (T2DM).

Methods: We analyzed a registry of 737 men (353 and 384 men on/not on TU, respectively) with adult-onset TD with nearly 9 years of follow-up. We compared associations between age and mortality using nonparametric and logistic regression models (estimating individual mortality probability) in men stratified by TU treatment and T2DM.

Results: Mortality was lower (p < 0.001) in men on TU compared to men opting against TU. In the men on TU, age was associated with mortality (odds ratio (OR): 1.26, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.40) in the nonlinear pattern expected in the Gompertz‒Makeham model. However, age was not associated with mortality in men not on TU (OR: 1.03, 95% CI: 0.98-1.08). T2DM status did not affect these associations.

Conclusion: The association between age and mortality differed between men on TU and those opting against treatment. In untreated men, features of metabolic syndrome worsened, which perhaps minimized the relationship between age and mortality. In men on TU, these metabolic risk factors improved, perhaps restoring the association between age and mortality.

papers.title: Styloidogenic Jugular Venous Compression Syndrome: A Rare Vascular Variant of Eagle Syndrome
abstract: Background and importance: Styloidogenic jugular venous compression syndrome, a recently recognized vascular variant of Eagle syndrome, a rare condition caused by the elongation of the styloid process or calcification of the stylohyoid ligament, occurs when the internal jugular vein is compressed between the styloid process and C1 transverse process, leading to a spectrum of neurovascular and cervicofacial symptoms.

Clinical presentation: A 46-year-old male pilot presented with right-sided pulsatile tinnitus, vertigo, and episodic near-syncope that progressively worsened over 4 years despite multiple interventions. Computed tomography and MRI revealed an elongated right styloid process (approximately 35 mm) compressing the internal jugular vein against the C1 transverse process. The patient underwent a right-sided styloidectomy with partial resection of the C1 transverse process by a transcervical approach. The facial and spinal accessory nerves were preserved, and postoperative recovery was uneventful. By postoperative day 2, the patient reported near-complete resolution of tinnitus and pain, with sustained improvement at 1-month follow-up.

Conclusion: Styloidogenic jugular venous compression syndrome should be considered for patients with pulsatile tinnitus or symptoms of impaired cerebral venous outflow. Computed tomography venography is considered the diagnostic gold standard. Surgical decompression through styloidectomy with C1 resection can provide effective and durable symptom relief. Early diagnosis and surgical management can result in excellent outcomes.

papers.title: Knowledge and Attitudes Toward Dementia Among Healthcare Professionals in the MENA Region: A Multinational Survey
abstract: BackgroundDementia is an escalating public health challenge in the MENA region, where primary healthcare professionals' (HCPs) knowledge and preparedness remain underexplored. Understanding their knowledge and attitudes is vital for early diagnosis, quality care, and effective awareness strategies.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study of 1224 HCPs across several Arab countries, primarily in primary care settings. Data were collected via an online survey using two validated instruments: the Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale (DKAS) and the Dementia Attitudes Scale (DAS).ResultsMost participants demonstrated moderate knowledge (68.5%), while 19.9% demonstrated poor knowledge and 11.5% demonstrated good knowledge. Attitudes were largely neutral to positive (44.1%). Multivariate analysis revealed that higher age predicted better knowledge (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.02-1.06, P < .001), while positive attitudes were significantly associated with older age (OR = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01-1.04, P = .002), female gender (OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.14-1.84, P = .003), and higher knowledge scores (OR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.17-1.28, P < .001).Conclusionmoderate knowledge and generally positive attitudes, important gaps persist. Tailored education, particularly for younger and male HCPs, is needed to improve dementia literacy and care.

papers.title: Targeting the gut-brain axis with Bifidobacterium breve in neurodegeneration: A comprehensive narrative review of current evidence in Alzheimer's disease and cognitive aging
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder arising from the interplay of amyloid, tau, neuroimmune, oxidative stress, metabolic, vascular, and synaptic processes, ultimately resulting in neurodegeneration across multiple brain regions and progressive memory and cognitive impairment. Gut dysfunction may contribute to the initiation and progression of AD-related processes through the gut-brain axis, whereby alterations in the gut microbiota can influence brain function through chemical, neuronal, immune, and metabolic pathways. Growing interest in the microbiota-gut-brain axis has consequently prompted investigation of strain-specific probiotics as potential adjunctive approaches to restoring gut microbial homeostasis. This comprehensive narrative review critically integrates preclinical and human evidence on Bifidobacterium breve in AD-related pathology and age-associated cognitive impairment. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were conducted through April 2026 and supplemented by reference-list searching. The evidence base comprised 13 preclinical publications and five human publications representing four independent clinical cohorts. Preclinical studies, predominantly conducted in rodent models, reported strain-dependent effects on cognition, amyloid- and tau-related measures, synaptic proteins, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, microbial composition, and metabolite profiles. Human evidence was limited to B. breve MCC1274 (A1) and primarily involved Japanese adults with memory complaints or suspected mild cognitive impairment. Overall, current evidence supports a mechanistic rationale for the potential role of B. breve as a gut-brain modulator; however, the heterogeneity of preclinical findings and the small, geographically concentrated clinical evidence base highlight the need for further well-designed studies to more clearly define clinical efficacy and long-term safety.

papers.title: Exploring emotion identification and categorisation in simulated central vision loss: an event-related potential study
abstract: Objective: This study investigated how simulated central vision loss (SimCVL) affected emotion identification and categorisation in individuals with normal vision.

Methods and analysis: The study recruited 29 healthy volunteers, including young adults (YA: 20–35 years) (n=10), mid-aged (MA: 40–55 years) (n=10) and older adults (60–75 years) (n=9). The participants were presented with human faces displaying three emotions, neutral, happy and sad, as stimuli. SimCVL was simulated using custom-made MATLAB programming. The study developed two experiments to investigate emotion identification (experiment 1: oddball design) and categorisation (experiment 2: equiprobable design). The behavioural responses and event-related potential (ERP) waveforms were analysed using E-prime and electroencephalogram laboratory toolbox in MATLAB, and the data was analysed using SPSS V.20.

Results: Emotion identification was present for both happy and sad in the Oddball (P300) paradigm. However, reduced amplitudes and delayed latencies were observed in OAs, particularly in simulated conditions (p<0.01). OAs had delayed reaction times and reduced accuracy in the simulated condition compared with MA and YA (p<0.01). No or minimal differences in amplitudes and latencies were found for early visual processing (P100) and encoding of facial features (N170) across age groups in simulated conditions. Delayed latencies and reduced amplitudes were observed in OAs when decoding (N250) facial features.

Conclusion: Emotion identification and categorisation are affected in older individuals with SimCVL compared with young and MA adults. Negative emotions had reduced performance index than happy across age groups, and this effect was maximum in OAs. The study suggests that further research is needed to explore the neural basis of emotional processing in patients with CVL using event-related potentials.

papers.title: A Standardized In Vitro Protocol for Evaluating Human Dental Pulp Stem Cell Differentiation and Proliferation on Nanomaterial Scaffolds
abstract: Reliable assessment of osteogenic and odontogenic differentiation, as well as stem cell proliferation, is fundamental to evaluating the biological performance of scaffold-based regenerative strategies. However, variability in experimental protocols, assay selection, and data interpretation often limits reproducibility and inter-study comparison. The protocol described in this article presents a standardized, reproducible workflow for the in vitro evaluation of osteogenic and odontogenic differentiation, as well as proliferative capacity, of stem cells cultured on biomaterial scaffolds. Osteogenic commitment is evaluated by alkaline phosphatase (ALP) enzymatic activity and Receptor Activator of Nuclear Factor κB Ligand (RANKL) immunofluorescence, while odontogenic commitment is assessed by DMP-1 (dentin matrix protein-1) immunofluorescence; both protein endpoints are quantified using standardized H-score methodology. Critical experimental parameters, including cell seeding density, induction timelines, assay conditions, normalization strategies (including protein-normalized ALP activity, cell-normalized 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) viability, and immunofluorescence H-score), and data analysis approaches, are detailed, along with troubleshooting guidance to minimize technical variability. The methodology has been applied as a standardized framework across multiple scaffold-based experimental studies, demonstrating robustness and reproducibility. By providing a comprehensive, validated framework, this article aims to facilitate standardized assessment of stem cell-scaffold interactions and improve comparability across preclinical regenerative studies.

papers.title: A causal atlas for sperm DNA fragmentation: separating "programmed" breaks from "acquired" injury across the male tract
abstract: Sperm DNA fragmentation (SDF) is still treated as a single metric despite converging evidence that it is a composite of mechanistically distinct break classes. We argue for a 'causal atlas' that maps when and where damage is introduced, from spermiogenesis to epididymal transit to ejaculation, and partitions SDF into programmed vulnerability created by faulty chromatin remodeling/topoisomerase-associated events and abortive apoptosis, versus acquired injury from oxidative/enzymatic attack during transit. Although current assays cannot definitively assign SDF to a particular mechanism or anatomical stage, integrating complementary measures may support mechanistically informed patient stratification and guide the development of more targeted interventions.

papers.title: Waterpipe Smoke Condensate Impairs p53 Nuclear Localization in Association with HIF-1α Stabilization
abstract: Waterpipe (shisha or hookah) smoking is recognized as a risk factor for lung cancer; however, its interference with hypoxia stress and tumor suppressor pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is poorly defined. In this study, NSCLC cell lines (A549, H460, H226 with endogenous wild-type p53, and H1299 transiently expressing wild-type or p53 mutants) were exposed to waterpipe smoke condensate (WPSC) under normoxic and/or hypoxic conditions. WPSC induced HIF-1α stabilization under normoxic conditions, accompanied by predominantly cytoplasmic localization and without corresponding induction of the canonical HIF-1 target genes examined. In parallel, WPSC transiently reduced nuclear p53 localization without altering total p53 protein levels. In A549 cells, WPSC pretreatment attenuated irradiation-induced expression of the p53 target genes cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A (CDKN1A) and BTG anti-proliferation factor 2 (BTG2). Pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1α partially restored nuclear p53 localization, supporting the involvement of HIF-1α in this response. Co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated an association between HIF-1α and p53 following WPSC exposure. Collectively, these findings show that WPSC-induced HIF-1α stabilization under normoxic conditions is associated with transient alterations in p53 localization and transcriptional response, supporting an involvement of HIF-1α in this process.

papers.title: Direct and Indirect Associations Between War-Related Nightmares, Anxiety-Depression Symptoms, and Somatization in a Sample of Displaced Lebanese Adults During the 2024-2025 Lebanese War: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background and aims: Somatization, the physical manifestation of emotional and psychological distress, is a prevalent issue in populations exposed to war and trauma. War-related nightmares are common among displaced individuals and are linked to depression, anxiety, and somatization. Yet, the indirect role of depression-anxiety in the association between war-related nightmares and somatization remains underexplored, particularly in the Lebanese context during the 2024-2025 war. This study aimed to examine whether war-related nightmares were associated with somatization both directly and indirectly through anxiety and depression considered simultaneously as parallel mediators among a sample of displaced Lebanese adults.

Methods: This cross-sectional study enrolled 294 displaced Lebanese adults (mean age 25.4 years; 72.1% female) through a convenience and snowball sampling technique (October 2024-March 2025) that made this study prone to selection bias. A parallel indirect-effect analysis was conducted using SPSS version 27 and PROCESS macro version 5.0, Model 4, with anxiety and depression entered simultaneously as parallel mediators. The model was adjusted for gender, occupation, and number of bombing exposures, and indirect effects were estimated using 5000 percentile-bootstrap samples.

Results: A significant total indirect association between war-related nightmares and somatization through anxiety and depression was observed (indirect effect: B = 0.14; Bootstrapped Standard Error = 0.04; Bootstrapped 95% Confidence Interval [0.07, 0.21]). The specific indirect association through depression was significant (B = 0.07; BootSE = 0.04; 95% Bootstrapped Confidence Interval [0.01; 0.15]), whereas the specific indirect association through anxiety was not significant (B = 0.06; BootSE = 0.04; 95% Bootstrapped Confidence Interval [-0.01; 0.14]). More frequent war-related nightmares were significantly associated with higher anxiety (B = 0.13; SE = 0.01, p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval [0.10, 0.16]) and higher depression (B = 0.12; SE = 0.01, p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval [0.09, 0.15]). When both mediators were entered simultaneously, depression was significantly associated with higher somatization (B = 0.58; SE = 0.28, p = 0.040; 95% Confidence Interval [0.03, 1.14]), whereas anxiety was not independently associated with somatization (B = 0.50; SE = 0.29, p = 0.088; 95% Confidence Interval [-0.07, 1.06]). War-related nightmares remained directly associated with somatization after accounting for both mediators (B = 0.42; SE = 0.06, p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval [0.30, 0.55]). The total association between war-related nightmares and somatization was B = 0.56 (SE = 0.06 p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval 0.45, 0.67).

Conclusion: War-related nightmares were associated with somatization both directly and indirectly through anxiety and depression collectively among a sample of displaced Lebanese adults. The specific indirect association through depression was significant, whereas the specific indirect association through anxiety was not. Although findings should be interpreted within the context of interrelated trauma symptoms and the cross-sectional design, which precludes temporal or causal conclusions, these results suggest a need for integrated mental health interventions addressing war-related nightmares, anxiety, depression, and somatic symptoms in war-affected populations.

papers.title: Neuraxial Medication Administration Errors During Anaesthesia and Perioperative Management, Consequences, Contributing Human and Systemic Factors and Their Prevention: A Systematic Review
abstract: Introduction: This systematic review aimed to investigate neuraxial administration errors, examine their contributing factors, and evaluate clinical outcomes using a novel harm scale.

Methods: The author searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, EBSCOhost, and Google Scholar for reports from 1981 to 2025 in any language. Exclusions were reviews, overdose incidents, and non-neuraxial administrations. Harm was classified using a novel five-level scale, and contributing factors were identified using the Human and Systemic Factors Analysis Classification System (HFACS).

Results: The search revealed 50 reports (54 patients), mainly involving the epidural route (38 vs 16 intrathecal), non-obstetric patients (35 vs 17 obstetric), and female gender (73%). Medications were grouped into nine divisions: IV fluids/total parenteral nutrition/insulin, anticholinergics, antiseptics, antiemetics, anticoagulants, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, opioids, Syntocinon, and others. Atropine (6 patients) was the most common, followed by remifentanil (4), Syntocinon (4), chlorhexidine (3), and water (3). Level 4 events (irreversible paraplegia or quadriplegia, 4 patients) and level 5 events (death, 4 patients) were mostly due to accidental antiseptic bolus administration. Inadvertent neuraxial drug administration occurred at different locations and during various stages of clinical care. The Human Factors Analysis Classification System (HFACS) identified unsafe acts related to skill-based errors and misidentification of routinely used objects. Additional deficiencies included organisational processes, resources, supervision, and task execution for neuraxial anaesthesia or analgesia.

Conclusions: Level 4 and 5 harm was mainly associated with the administration of antiseptic solutions. The HFACS framework-based analysis suggested multiple modifiable institutional and individual deficiencies. Multidisciplinary improvements of organisational safety procedures, relevant preconditions, and neuraxial clinical practices may help prevent these serious incidents.

papers.title: AI-assisted peer review: efficiency for reviewers, burden for authors-a narrative review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in scholarly peer review has the potential to simplify the work of editors and reviewers through faster triage, automated reporting completeness checks, and scalable synthesis of reviewer comments. However, it also presents practical, ethical, and technical limitations that may place implementation burdens on authors. I examine bias arising from training data and model architecture, confidentiality risks from commercial AI deployment, accountability gaps when human judgment is displaced, and the growing threat of hallucinated citations to scientific integrity. I further analyze how poorly governed AI integration shifts remediation and formatting burdens onto authors-particularly those from under-resourced or non-Western institutions. I propose hybrid human-AI workflows, mandatory disclosure standards, and equity-conscious implementation frameworks to address these harms. Responsible AI integration in peer review requires transparency, human accountability, and deliberate protection of the diversity of voices represented in scientific literature. These considerations also extend beyond individual actors to recursive feedback loops in which AI-assisted manuscripts are evaluated by AI-assisted review systems, reinforcing the need for human contextual stewardship.

papers.title: Physical Activity, Myokine-Adipokine Signatures and Haemoglobin Glycation Index in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Background: The Hemoglobin Glycation Index (HGI) reflects variability in hemoglobin glycation beyond ambient glycaemia and is a marker of metabolic heterogeneity, cardiovascular risk and treatment response in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Whether circulating myokines and adipokines are related to HGI, or whether relationships differ across exercise modalities, is unclear.

Objective: To examine associations of circulating myokines (irisin, myostatin, myonectin, IL-6, IL-15) and adipokines (leptin, adiponectin) with HGI, and whether associations differ between physically active and sedentary individuals and across exercise modalities.

Methods: Cross-sectional study of 185 adults with T2DM recruited at Thumbay Hospital, Ajman, United Arab Emirates, classified as physically active (n=98) or sedentary (n=87), with active individuals sub-grouped by predominant modality: aerobic (70), resistance (11), combined (17). Measurements were obtained after an overnight fast. HGI was calculated as the residual of HbA1c regressed on fasting plasma glucose. Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Spearman correlations with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and median regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and fasting glucose were used.

Results: Active participants had lower HGI than sedentary participants (median -0.44 vs 0.12; p = 0.001), with lower BMI, fasting glucose and HbA1c. HGI differed by modality (p < 0.001), most favourable in the combined-training group and least favourable in the aerobic-only group. IL-6 was inversely correlated with HGI in active participants and leptin in sedentary participants (both FDR p < 0.05). Physical activity remained an independent predictor of lower HGI after adjustment for age, sex and BMI (β = -0.65;p< 0.001), and persisted after adjustment for IL-15 and leptin.

Conclusion: Precludes causal inference; if confirmed prospectively, associations may inform individualized exercise prescription and HGI-based risk stratification.Distinct myokine-adipokine signatures were associated with glycation variability beyond mean glycaemia and combined aerobic-plus-resistance training with the most favourable HGI profile. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; if confirmed prospectively, associations may inform individualized exercise prescription and HGI-based risk stratification.

papers.title: Relative accuracy of intraoral photogrammetry and intraoral scanning with conventional scan-body for full-arch implants
abstract: Purpose: To compare the relative accuracy of intraoral photogrammetry (IPG) and intraoral scan (IOS) with conventional scan bodies (IOS-CB) for complete-arch implant impressions, using the conventional splinted open-tray impression digitized with a laboratory scanner (COT-LS) as the reference standard.

Materials and methods: Twenty-six edentulous maxillary arches restored with four BioHorizons Tapered Internal implants supporting multiunit abutments were included. For each patient, three impressions were obtained: (1) a conventional splinted open-tray impression poured in type IV dental stone and scanned with a laboratory extraoral scanner to generate the COT-LS dataset; (2) an IOS-CB using the Aoralscan Elite, with scan bodies present from the outset of a single continuous scanning pass; and (3) an IPG scan using the same device in photogrammetry mode with dedicated scan flags mounted on the multiunit abutments. STL files were analyzed in Geomagic Control X, with the COT-LS dataset used as the reference. Relative accuracy was quantified as centroid-based linear deviation from COT-LS following best-fit alignment. Measurement reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) from two independent examiners analyzing the same datasets. The IOS-CB and IPG datasets were superimposed to calculate linear and three-dimensional positional deviations (µm). A repeated-measures two-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc testing was performed (p < 0.05).

Results: IPG demonstrated significantly lower deviations than IOS-CB in the full-arch, anterior right, and anterior left regions (p < 0.001). IOS-CB showed significantly lower deviations than IPG in both posterior right and posterior left regions (p < 0.001). The full-arch mean deviation was lower for IPG (39.2 µm) than IOS-CB (45.1 µm). All deviations for both techniques remained within the clinically acceptable threshold for passive fit. ICC values for measurement reproducibility exceeded 0.95 for both techniques.

Conclusions: Within the limitations of this clinical study, IPG demonstrated a lower full-arch mean deviation than IOS-CB when evaluated against the COT-LS reference. However, as the inherent dimensional error of the COT-LS reference may approach or exceed the 5.9 µm between-technique difference, this finding should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory evidence of a trueness advantage. Measurement reproducibility was high for both techniques (ICC >0.95).

papers.title: Mediating Effect of Perceived Ageism Experiences Between TikTok Addiction Symptoms and Psychological Distress: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background and aims: TikTok addiction has been linked to depression and anxiety, yet mechanisms underlying this relationship remain underexplored. Based on the Social Comparison and Uses and Gratifications theories, this study examined whether perceived ageism experiences mediate the relationship between TikTok addiction and depression and anxiety among Lebanese adults. The research also explores, as a theoretical possibility, whether TikTok's algorithm may be associated with greater perceived ageism experiences, which in turn would relate to psychological distress.

Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 855 participants (mean age 24.39; 76.7% females) using the TikTok Addiction Test, WHO Ageism Scale, and PHQ-4. Data were analyzed using SPSS and mediation analysis via PROCESS Macro controlling for demographic and health covariates, such as gender, education level and a history of mental health diagnosis. The mediation analysis included 735 participants with complete data for all variables entered into the model.

Results: TikTok addiction was positively associated with psychological distress. Perceived ageism experiences partially mediated this relationship (unstandardized indirect effect: B = 0.0149, BootSE = 0.005, 95% percentile bootstrapped CI [0.0058, 0.0255]). Higher TikTok addiction symptoms were associated with greater perceived ageism experiences, which were in turn associated with higher psychological distress levels. Demographic analysis showed that females, those with lower levels of education and individuals with a history of mental health diagnosis reported higher psychological distress. Age was negatively correlated with psychological distress, showcasing higher vulnerability among younger individuals.

Conclusion: Findings highlight perceived ageism experiences as a small but statistically significant mediator between addictive digital media use and psychological distress. The study emphasizes the need for culturally sensitive mental health and digital literacy interventions, as they aim to support the deconstruction of idealized youthful standards, particularly with the Lebanese context where digital media serves as escapism.

papers.title: Three-Point Bedside Congestion Score (IJV Collapsibility + IVC Collapsibility + Central Venous Pressure) in Elective Mitral Valve Surgery: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Background: Systemic venous congestion and right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction are key drivers of postoperative hemodynamic instability, prolonged ventilation, and acute kidney injury (AKI) after mitral valve surgery. Comprehensive echocardiography is informative but may be impractical in high-throughput pre-anesthesia workflows. We evaluated a pragmatic three-point bedside congestion score combining internal jugular vein (IJV) collapsibility, inferior vena cava (IVC) collapsibility, and invasively measured central venous pressure (CVP) for preoperative risk stratification.

Methods: In this prospective, observational, single-center study, 100 consecutive adults (>18 years) undergoing elective mitral valve surgery for mitral stenosis were enrolled. A bedside ultrasound was performed in the preoperative area with patients in a 45° head-elevated position during quiet, spontaneous respiration. One point was assigned for each abnormal component (IJV collapsibility <18%, IVC collapsibility <25%, and CVP >12 mmHg), yielding a total score of 0 to 3. Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) was dichotomized at 17 mm. Outcomes included vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay, AKI, and in-hospital mortality. Discrimination for AKI and mortality was evaluated using a 5-fold cross-validated receiver operating characteristic (ROC) area under the curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Calibration was assessed using recalibration intercept and slope, and decision curve analysis was used to explore clinical net benefit across threshold probabilities.

Results: The observed score distribution concentrated at 0 to 2 and 3; therefore, patients were analyzed as low score (0 to 2; n = 50) versus high score (3; n = 50). Compared with low-score patients, high-score patients had higher postoperative VIS (median 18.0 vs 10.0), longer ventilation (31.5 vs 22.0 hours), longer ICU stay (10.0 vs 5.5 days), and longer hospital stay (23.0 vs 12.5 days). AKI occurred in 40% versus 20%, and mortality in 10% versus 2% in high- versus low-score groups. In the combined 2 × 2 stratification, low score with normal TAPSE had no AKI or mortality, whereas high score with abnormal TAPSE had AKI in 55.6% and mortality in 14.8%. The combined score + TAPSE model showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.77 for AKI; AUC 0.782 for mortality) with near-ideal calibration in this dataset. Decision curve analysis suggested a higher net benefit for the combined model than single-predictor models across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05 to 0.30.

Conclusions: A simple three-point bedside congestion score stratifies postoperative risk after elective mitral valve surgery. Incorporating TAPSE into preoperative assessment provided a rapid and reliable means of excluding significant RV dysfunction, thereby reinforcing the validity of the threepoint scoring system. Multicenter external validation and evaluation of score-guided perioperative protocols are warranted.

papers.title: Safety and efficacy of indigenous ultrathin-strut versus international thin-strut drug-eluting coronary stents in percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Introduction: Ultrathin-strut drug-eluting stents (DES) have been developed to enhance vascular healing and reduce restenosis following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Indigenous biodegradable-polymer ultrathin-strut DES are increasingly used in high-burden settings; however, comparative evidence against internationally established thin-strut DES remains limited.

Methods: This systematic review of randomized controlled trials was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to December 2025. Trials comparing indigenous ultrathin-strut DES with internationally manufactured thin-strut DES in adult PCI populations were included. Primary outcomes were major adverse cardiac events/trial-defined composite endpoints. Secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction, target lesion and vessel revascularization, stent thrombosis, cardiac death, and all-cause mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB-2 tool, and a narrative synthesis was performed.

Results: Four randomized trials including 2,793 patients were analyzed. Indigenous stents demonstrated comparable rates of composite endpoints, myocardial infarction, repeat revascularization, and stent thrombosis across studies, with no consistent differences between groups.

Conclusion: The available RCT evidence shows no consistent signal of superiority or inferiority between indigenous and international thin-strut DES. However, heterogeneity and limited trial numbers warrant larger studies with long-term follow-up and real-world materiovigilance.
